metadata.directionPolicy: For manifestation -> concept, broadMatch means the target concept is broader; narrowMatch means the target concept is narrower.
metadata.reviewPolicy: Concept mappings support discovery and source-aware comparison. They never authorize pooling or aggregation unless aggregationSafe is explicitly true.

concepts.label: Full immunization coverage
concepts.definition: Coverage of a specified child population completing the vaccination schedule defined by the relevant source and period.

mappings.rationale: The routine HMIS manifestation measures the same broad construct, but uses estimated children below one year, children aged 9–11 months in the numerator and a historical antigen schedule.

The programme scorecard manifestation compares fully immunised children aged 9–11 months with children of the same age due for immunisation, but the cited table does not publish a complete operational formula.
The survey-based scorecard label represents the same broad construct but applies to children aged 12–23 months and does not publish a computation in the cited table.
The household-survey manifestation is conceptually aligned, but differs from routine reporting in sampling, recall or card evidence, survey reference period and the survey-defined vaccination series.

concepts.label: Immunization session plan adherence
concepts.definition: Whether planned immunization sessions were held in the specified geography and monitoring period.

mappings.rationale: This is the closest percentage manifestation of sessions conducted among sessions planned, but the registry record does not preserve the operational form, exclusions or monitoring period needed for pooling.
The official IMI item is a count of sessions held as planned. It supports adherence analysis but is not itself an adherence proportion without a planned-session denominator.
This is a narrower manifestation restricted to monitored high-risk areas and planned sessions actually selected for monitoring; the target concept is broader.

concepts.label: Vaccine availability at immunization sessions
concepts.definition: Availability or absence of required vaccines at planned or monitored immunization sessions.

mappings.rationale: Stock-out is directionally inverse to availability and may use a different vaccine basket, observation window and session denominator; it should not be treated as a direct synonym.
The IMI monitoring item directly assesses vaccine availability, but the source list does not specify the numerator rule, required vaccine basket or treatment of partial availability.
Reason analysis explains non-availability among affected sessions; it is a categorical diagnostic, not an availability measure.

concepts.label: AEFI surveillance performance
concepts.definition: Performance of adverse-event reporting, documentation, investigation, completion and causality-classification processes.

mappings.rationale: Reported AEFI case count reflects surveillance output and event occurrence, not performance by itself; a higher count is not unambiguously better or worse.
Line-listing completeness is one narrower documentation component of the broader AEFI surveillance-performance concept.
Timely reporting of serious AEFI cases is one narrower timeliness component of the broader performance concept.
Timely sharing of the Case Reporting Form is one narrower documentation-flow component of the broader performance concept.
Timely investigation of serious cases is one narrower investigation-timeliness component of the broader performance concept.
Completed investigation is one narrower completeness component of the broader performance concept and is distinct from investigation timeliness.
Timely causality classification by the relevant committee is one narrower endpoint component of the broader surveillance-performance concept.

concepts.label: Immunization dropout
concepts.definition: Failure to complete a defined vaccination sequence among children who received an earlier dose or antigen.

mappings.rationale: The historical HMIS BCG-to-measles dropout percentage is a narrower antigen-pair manifestation; the target dropout concept is broader.
The historical HMIS DPT3-to-measles dropout percentage is a narrower antigen-pair manifestation; the target dropout concept is broader.
Absolute dropout count supports programme action but is not equivalent to a percentage and cannot be compared without the first-dose cohort size.
BCG-to-Penta-3 dropout is a narrower antigen-pair manifestation of the broader dropout concept.
Penta-1-to-Penta-3 dropout is a narrower within-series manifestation of the broader dropout concept.
BCG-to-MCV1 dropout is a narrower antigen-pair manifestation of the broader dropout concept.
